paper.title: Reinforcement Learning for Self-Improving Agent with Skill Library
paper.central_claim: SAGE (Skill Augmented GRPO for self-Evolution), combining Sequential Rollout over chains of similar tasks and a Skill-integrated Reward, trains a skill-library agent to generate and reuse executable skills; on AppWorld it gains 8.9 SGC points over GRPO while using 26% fewer steps and 59% fewer tokens.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; worker read full text incl. appendices A-L; no page images provided.

rationale: 边界模式：RL训练写/用技能的 improver，非权重技能库留存；有技能开关与奖励消融和留出划分，但技能库仅限同场景三任务、依赖场景标签与专家SFT。

evidence.quote: achieves 8.9% higher Scenario Goal Completion while requiring 26% fewer interaction steps and generating 59% fewer tokens
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim (vs author GRPO baseline).
RL baseline without skill library (Test-Normal TGC 69.2 / SGC 51.8; Challenge 40.7 / 26.9).
SAGE: Test-Normal 72.0 / 60.7; Test-Challenge 50.1 / 32.4.
SFT-only stage (Claude-3.5 expert trajectories).
Prompt-only skill library agent underperforms plain ReAct (39.2 TGC) - evidence for the author gap.
Reported (not rerun) RL baseline without skills: TGC 71.3 close to SAGE 72.0.
Skills on/off for the SAGE model: SGC 60.7 vs 54.8 (+5.9), TGC 72.0 vs 71.4 (+0.6).

evidence.quote: all agent models achieve improved SGC scores with reduced average steps and tokens when employing skills compared to no skill settings
evidence.support_explanation: Retained-library ablation exists for every stage.

evidence.quote: However, we observe a decline in TGC scores for Skill Library Agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Skills hurt TGC for the untrained agent (34.7 -> 30.7).

evidence.quote: rewards signal from the successful usage of skills in later tasks can be back-propagated to the skill generation in the previous tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Credit path from later-task use to earlier skill generation (H26 core).

evidence.quote: we construct the sequential tasks with examples under the same scenario, in which all tasks share similar instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Chain tasks are near-duplicate instructions by construction.

evidence.quote: If the skill can be executed without error, add the new skill or update the existing skill in the skill library
evidence.support_explanation: Only admission gate: executes without error.
Reward-design ablation: skill-integrated reward best on TGC/SGC.

evidence.quote: we employed an idealized case during sequential rollout where skills are retained and utilized only within the same scenario in the task chain
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval idealized as same-scenario.

evidence.quote: While our default evaluation uses the ideal case (Same Scenario) with provided scenario labels from the test set
evidence.support_explanation: Default evaluation uses scenario labels from the test set (privileged grouping).
Label-free retrieval variants recover most of the gain; N-gram exploits near-identical in-scenario queries.

evidence.quote: Although our final results rely on SFT using expert experience data generated by Claude
evidence.support_explanation: Result depends on expert SFT initialisation.
Matched SFT-initialised GRPO baseline (skill library not engaged) is below SAGE.

evidence.quote: Therefore, we implemented our own baseline training using the GRPO method without Skill Library for comparison purposes.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline is the authors' own GRPO run (LOOP not reproducible).

evidence.quote: The Dev set guides the best checkpoint selection during training.
evidence.support_explanation: Train / Dev (checkpoint) / Test split.

evidence.quote: The Test-Challenge set not only contains more test examples but also requires APIs from applications (Amazon and Gmail) that are absent from the Train, Dev, and Test-Normal sets.
evidence.support_explanation: Test-Challenge is out-of-distribution on APIs.

evidence.quote: All reported numbers in this paper represent the average of three agent evaluation runs using the same model.
evidence.support_explanation: Three evaluation runs of one trained model; no training-seed variance.

evidence.quote: We performed the whole RL training process on 4xNVIDIA H100 8-GPU nodes.
evidence.support_explanation: Training hardware stated; no GPU-hours or total token cost.

evidence.quote: resulting in totally 288 rollout
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline GRPO uses 288 rollouts per step; SAGE uses 384 per step with doubled sequential length.

evidence.quote: they predominantly rely on manually crafted prompts for skill generation and utilization
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: prompt-driven skill generation/use.

evidence.quote: This prompt-based approach, however, is inherently constrained by the instruction following capabilities of the base model, limiting both the quality and adaptability of the skill library.
evidence.support_explanation: Gap restated; supported by E005.

evidence.quote: Initial RL experiments with open-source models revealed their limited capabilities in following instructions when integrated with our skill library agent, despite carefully designed prompts.
evidence.support_explanation: Prompting insufficient for open models, motivating SFT+RL.

evidence.quote: we conducted experiments exclusively on the AppWorld dataset
evidence.support_explanation: Single benchmark.

evidence.quote: SAGE significantly improves both Skill Usage Rate and Success Skill Usage Rate compared to previous steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Skill-use diagnostics improve after RL.

evidence.quote: Importantly, each skill library is constrained to its specific task scenario.
evidence.support_explanation: No cross-scenario library accumulation in default evaluation; no retirement or growth control needed or tested.

evidence.quote: Given these challenges and the empirically suboptimal performance, we ultimately chose a two-example task chain structure.
evidence.support_explanation: Longer chains tested and rejected (SGC 54.8 vs 60.7).

evidence.quote: This process finally yielded 1,129 valid examples.
evidence.support_explanation: Expert SFT set size (rejection sampling, Claude Sonnet 3.5 V2).

gap.author_gap: Skill-library agents rely on manually crafted prompts for skill generation and use, limited by base-model instruction following; RL-trained agents are tied to training scenarios and do not exploit on-going experience in new environments.
gap.checked_gap: Supported by the paper's own control: the prompt-only skill library agent underperforms plain ReAct (TGC 30.7 vs 39.2) with the same base model. The absence of RL-for-skill-library prior work is asserted, not searched.

claims.text: SAGE outperforms existing approaches in accuracy and efficiency (SGC +8.9, steps -26%, tokens -59%) on AppWorld.
claims.setting: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct; Test-Normal 168 / Test-Challenge 417; three evaluation runs
claims.baseline_control: author GRPO (no skills, no SFT), SFT-initialised GRPO, LOOP (reported), ReAct
claims.selection_vs_test: Dev for checkpoint; skills accumulate within each test scenario using scenario labels
claims.result_denominator: SGC 60.7 vs 51.8 (Normal), 32.4 vs 26.9 (Challenge); TGC 72.0 vs 69.2, 50.1 vs 40.7
claims.allowed_conclusion: On AppWorld, SAGE (expert-SFT + RL with sequential rollout) beats the authors' own GRPO and SFT-GRPO; TGC advantage over reported LOOP is within noise; gain needs expert SFT and larger rollout budget.

claims.text: The retained skill library contributes to the gain (agent self-improves via skills).
claims.setting: same model with empty vs accumulating skill library, Test-Normal
claims.selection_vs_test: skills from earlier tasks of the same test scenario
claims.result_denominator: SAGE SGC 60.7 vs 54.8; TGC 72.0 vs 71.4; steps 12.1 vs 16.0; SFT stage SGC 41.7 vs 39.9
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within a three-task near-duplicate scenario, skills add ~+6 SGC and cut steps; no evidence of cross-scenario library benefit or long-run library growth.

claims.text: The Skill-integrated Reward is better than outcome-only or chain-only rewards.
claims.selection_vs_test: same training data and Dev selection
claims.allowed_conclusion: Skill-aware reward helps SGC by ~4-5 points with std ~1.5 (single trained model per variant).

claims.text: RL is needed beyond prompting or SFT for a skill library agent.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Both SFT and RL steps raise performance in this pipeline.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On AppWorld with Qwen2.5-32B, an expert-SFT-then-SAGE-trained skill-library agent beats the authors' own GRPO and SFT-GRPO baselines on SGC and efficiency, and the same weights gain ~6 SGC points and 4 fewer steps from an accumulating same-scenario skill library; Test-Challenge also improves (author_report).
cannot_say: gains generalise beyond AppWorld or beyond same-scenario near-duplicate tasks
TGC gain over reported LOOP is significant
assessment.note: author_report only; no reproduction or our_run. Weight training is the improver; scope judged on the retained non-weight skill library.

G.reason: 具体问题有来源且被自身数据印证：提示式技能库依赖基座指令遵循（原型 Skill Library Agent TGC 30.7 低于 ReAct 39.2），RL 训练的 agent 难以持续利用部署经验；最近邻（Voyager/AWM/ASI/DynaSaur、LOOP）有对照；未覆盖更多同期 RL+技能工作，残余缺口（跨场景库、真实检索）已自陈。

M.reason: 操作、信息与假设可重建：技能生成/使用/更新/保存→序贯两任务链→后任务成功使用技能向前任务生成回传奖励，对应“下游使用计功”的 H26 逻辑；与结果奖励/链奖励替代有可区分预测（Tab 4）；弱点：使用指示符不区分技能真实贡献，链仅2步。

X.reason: 技能操作与奖励公式、检索和训练流程描述清楚；但准入仅“执行不报错”（无任务级重放/泛化验证）、无退役/版本/冲突处理、库仅限同场景三任务，默认检索依赖测试集场景标签，保留机制的适用条件与迁移边界不清。

E.measurement.reason: AppWorld 状态型单元测试给出 TGC/SGC，验证器可信，另测步数/token；技能使用率指标仅在使用技能的样本上定义，且 SGC 受同场景近重复任务影响。

E.causality.reason: 每阶段技能开/关消融（SAGE: SGC +5.9，TGC +0.6）、奖励设计、初始化、检索方式、链长及 SFT 初始化 GRPO 对照齐全；缺口：RL 预算不对等（384 vs 288 rollout，序贯翻倍时长）、对 GRPO 的大部分 TGC 增益并非来自技能库，训练种子单次。

E.holdout.reason: 官方 Train/Dev/Test 划分，Dev 选 checkpoint，Test-Challenge 含训练未见 API（Amazon/Gmail）；扣分点：默认评测用测试集场景标签做检索、同场景任务指令近乎相同、仅 AppWorld，故“新环境持续改进”的范围窄于主张。

E.statistics.reason: 全表给出三次评测运行的均值±std，部分增益大于 std（SGC +5.9 vs 0.8–1.5）；但仅评测重复、单次训练、无显著性检验或训练种子方差，TGC +0.6 在噪声内。

E.cost.reason: 报告推理步数/token（-26%、-59%）并说明训练硬件与 rollout 数；未给总训练/专家数据生成成本，SAGE 每步 384 rollout 且链序贯翻倍，与 GRPO 288 rollout 预算不等。
